title: Derby success metric: rank by distance-to-100% (lookahead4 black-win + white-non-loss), not saturated anchored elo
description:
WHY (Jason-gated v9 reframe, 2026-05-27): anchored elo SATURATES (~1700) because a draw scores 0.5 — so a model that DRAWS the hard games maxes elo without WINNING them. That is why v8 read 'nothing moves the needle': the metric is blind to the real gap. The true objective is 100% across the 3 in-repo evals = ALWAYS WINS as BLACK and NEVER LOSES as WHITE. Champion is NOT there: vs lookahead4 it is 4-0-6 BLACK (six draws) / 2-0-8 WHITE. White + heuristic + lookahead2 already meet 100%; the ENTIRE remaining gap is converting lookahead4 BLACK-DRAWS to WINS.

WHAT: add a 'distance-to-100%' / '100%-score' the derby ranks + allocates by, computed from the ALREADY-shipped color-split eval fields (eval/vs_<baseline>_black_w/l/d, white_w/l/d, from gi7). Suggested score per checkpoint = mean over the 3 baselines of [black_winrate + white_nonloss_rate]/2 (or, since the binding gap is narrow, surface lookahead4_black_winrate explicitly). The derby's pick_priority / Delta-elo-rate should hill-climb THIS, not anchored model_elo, near the ceiling — else v9's bigger models get judged by the saturated ruler and look 'equal' again.

ALSO (pairs with this): raise eval games-per-baseline (esp. vs lookahead4) so '100% / never-loses' is statistically real, not a lucky 0-loss-in-10.

SCOPE: delo_derby.py scoring/priority + the eval aggregation (run_sweep/eval_worker). Color-split data already exists (gi7, merged). This is the KEY v9 enabler — the scale-ladder cells (derby-v9-medium/large) need it to be judged correctly. Runner/orchestrator domain (touches the derby's GPU-scoring loop).
acceptance_criteria: Derby reports + ranks by a 100%-distance metric derived from the color-split eval fields (black-win-rate + white-non-loss-rate across heuristic/lookahead2/lookahead4); near-ceiling allocation follows lookahead4 black-win-rate, not saturated anchored elo; eval games-per-baseline raised enough that 'never-loses-white / wins-all-black' is statistically meaningful.
notes: THIRD requirement surfaced by the report_100pct.py read (2026-05-27): the color-split eval LAGS training badly — derby-v9-large has only 5 color-split evals (elo 339-788) while trained to ~1455. derby-i5j moved the frequent elo readout to per-chunk wandb but the color-split (the 100%-metric source) stayed sparse. So beyond (1) rank-by-distance-to-100% + (2) ~50-100 games/color, ADD (3) run the color-split vs-baselines eval at CURRENT strength / often enough (a current-checkpoint color-split on each matured lane). Without (3) the v9 scale verdict is unreadable regardless of net maturity. The metric is implemented as scripts/report_100pct.py (read-only, adoptable).

title: Cross-game store runaway: cap the dict to opening plies (ply < ~10)
description:
BUG (live runaway, follow-on to derby-eda): derby-x-crossgame's time/epoch_s climbs convexly ~1s -> ~48s over epochs 13-35.

NOT a game-length issue: plies stay ~15-32 and even DROP to 15 by e35 (decisive games, not full-board draws). NOT sgd (fixed 64). ROOT CAUSE: the cross-game position-stats store grows unbounded (116k -> 234k entries in one 300s slice), and position_stats.save() -> _renormalize() folds the lazy `scale` over EVERY entry on EVERY epoch (train.py:1467; position_stats.py _renormalize is O(store-size)). derby-eda made DECAY O(1) but save() re-introduced the O(N) per-epoch traversal -> as the store doubles, per-epoch save doubles -> convex wall growth.

FIX (Jason's call, and the principled one): cap the cross-game dict to OPENING positions only -- ply < N (default ~10). The ring buffer already carries `ply`; gate the ingest/aggregation so only positions with ply < cross_game_max_ply are stored. Mid/late-game positions are not added.

WHY this is the right fix, not just a perf patch:
- The opening is the MOST-transited region of the tree -> by far the richest cross-game transposition counts -> that's where the aggregate is statistically meaningful. Mid/late-game positions are near-unique singletons: they bloat the store with low-value entries AND are exactly what makes save() O(N).
- It bounds the store to the small, finite set of distinct openings -> O(N) save stays cheap forever; runaway gone; no compaction tuning needed.
- It directly serves the original motivation (the model not converging on optimal OPENINGS): concentrate the de-noised cross-game value signal precisely on opening positions.

IMPLEMENTATION:
- Add --cross-game-max-ply (default 10).
- In the train.py ingest path, only aggregate positions with ply < cross_game_max_ply.
- Relabel-on-sample is unchanged in logic: positions whose key is not in the (now opening-only) store fall back to single-game z. So only openings get the cross-game blend; everything else is baseline.
- Resume rebuild-from-buffer must respect the ply cap.
- OFF (no --cross-game-value) stays byte-identical.
- SECONDARY (optional, belt-and-suspenders): stop calling _renormalize() in save() every epoch -- renormalize only on scale-underflow. The ply cap alone fixes the runaway (store is now tiny), so this is not required.

DELIVERABLE: patch gomoku/position_stats.py + gomoku/train.py + the derby-x-crossgame cell (add "--cross-game-max-ply","10" to extra_train_args). NO GPU run in this bead. After merge, the runner re-races derby-x-crossgame.

ACCEPTANCE: store size PLATEAUS (opening-only, a few k entries) as games accumulate instead of growing to 200k+; time/epoch flat across a slice; only ply<cap positions ingested (test); relabel still correct for opening positions (test); resume rebuild respects the cap (test); --cross-game-value OFF byte-identical; py_compile run_sweep.py OK; tests/test_cross_game_value.py green.
acceptance_criteria: Store size plateaus (opening-only, ~few k entries) as games accumulate instead of growing to 200k+; time/epoch flat across a slice; only ply<cap positions ingested (test); relabel correct for openings (test); resume rebuild respects cap (test); --cross-game-value OFF byte-identical; py_compile run_sweep.py OK; tests/test_cross_game_value.py green. NO GPU run.
close_reason: Capped cross-game store to opening plies (ply<max_ply, default 10) + decoupled _renormalize() from save(). New --cross-game-max-ply flag threaded into PositionStats; live ingest gates on e.ply, resume rebuild gates on the buffer ply column; relabel falls back to single-game z outside the store. save() now persists raw counts + live scale verbatim (renorm only on underflow). Cell derby-x-crossgame gains --cross-game-max-ply 10. Verified CPU: store plateaus at the opening alphabet (40,641 late singletons ingested, store stays 60) while save/epoch flat (0.168ms->0.171ms); OFF-path byte-identical; tests/test_cross_game_value.py 33 passed. Merged feat/crossgame-plycap into main (4fdb402..dbf5864) and pushed. NO GPU run.

title: Fix derby-x-crossgame sidecar: O(store-size) per-epoch ingest (runaway slowdown)
description: The cross-game value sidecar (cell derby-x-crossgame, --cross-game-value) has a per-epoch cost that scales with STORE SIZE, not new-positions. Observed in Derby v8 (2026-05-27): epoch wall grew monotonically 14s->21->32->60->81->113->128s as position_stats.pkl grew to 14MB, while gen+train stayed ~10s. Net: the lane did ~47 epochs in 2 chunks (vs ~150+ for normal lanes) and was stuck at elo 389-711 — a MEASUREMENT ARTIFACT (slow training), not necessarily a bad idea. CODE-ONLY fix (NO GPU run): make the ingest/blend O(new positions) — incremental/amortized aggregation, and/or a bounded/compacted store (cap keys, periodic compaction, or use --cross-game-recency-decay to actually prune cold entries). Keep the store TRAINER-OWNED single-writer + lane-isolated (clean A/B). Deliverable: the existing derby-x-crossgame cell trains at ~normal epoch speed (~3s) so the derby runner can re-race it. Verify with a short smoke that epoch wall stays flat as the store grows. external_ref=claude-session:55038670-b85a-4bb6-b41f-002828592c5e

title: Defensive exact-solver teacher: relabel positions that concede a forced loss (the 'white' arm)
description:
The NOVEL half of the loss-tail epic. Our exact teacher (VCF today, VCT planned) proves forced WINS for the side to move -- pure attack. It NEVER teaches DEFENSE: the move that avoids conceding the opponent a forced win. That is exactly the "never-lose as white" half of the goal, and there is no prior bead and no prior wiki analysis of it.

WHAT: during the self-play teacher pass, after our move run the exact solver (VCF, then VCT) from the OPPONENT's perspective. If the opponent has a PROVEN forced win:
  - VALUE relabel (cheap, ship first): our position's true value = -1, overwrite the MCTS estimate (the exact mirror of the VCF value-stamp).
  - POLICY relabel (richer, second): search our OTHER legal moves for one that does NOT concede a forced win. If found, down-weight the played (losing) move and credit the refutation. If EVERY move loses, it is a true forced loss -- value -1 stands, no policy change.

WHY THIS AVOIDS THE KNOWN TRAP: opponent-mix / training-vs-baseline collapsed value-loss to 0.04 (defense-blindness) because it made the OPPONENT harder. This bead does NOT touch the opponent -- it keeps pure self-play and only RELABELS positions with exact defensive truth. Defensive signal without the training collapse.

CORRECTNESS (critical): same bar as VCF/VCT. A false "opponent has a forced win" poisons value targets in the WRONG direction. Must pass a 400-fuzz-vs-independent-referee gate (mirror of derby-y8r) before any race. Reuse the referee harness.

CLI: --defense-teacher (value-only mode), then --defense-teacher-policy (refutation mode). Code-only bead, NO GPU -- the derby runner races it once landed.

ACCEPTANCE: cuts WHITE-side loss-rate vs lookahead:depth=4 toward 0 without regressing black-side win-rate, and beats the vcf+global-pool+value-discount base head-to-head.
design: Value-only mode first (overwrite z=-1 when opponent has a proven forced win after our move); policy-refutation mode second (search our other legal moves for one that does not concede). Pure self-play relabel only -- never strengthen the opponent (that path collapsed vl to 0.04). CLI: --defense-teacher, then --defense-teacher-policy.
acceptance_criteria: Cuts white-side loss-rate vs lookahead:depth=4 toward 0 without regressing black-side win-rate; beats the vcf+global-pool+value-discount base head-to-head. Passes a 400-fuzz vs independent-referee correctness gate before any race.
close_reason: Shipped: value-only defensive exact-solver teacher (--defense-teacher). Relabel z=-1 when opponent has a proven VCF win via swapped-plane solve_vcf (no new solver). Gen-cost gate: skip-when-offense-fired + cheap has_four_threat pre-scan (quiet positions = ZERO solver recursion). 400-fuzz vs independent referee = ZERO false positives (6 real lines verified, non-vacuous). Byte-identical when off (verified). Cell derby-x-defense (champion+defense). Merged 22d8a82 (branch feat/defense-teacher). Policy/refutation mode deferred (defense non-unique). Live gen-cost under flooding to be confirmed by the runner's full-load epoch-50+ re-race per the ingest-perf-flooding lesson.

title: Kill the depth-4 loss-tail: 100% black / never-lose white via exact-solver teaching
description:
GOAL: drive our net's tactical loss-tail to zero. Our strongest checkpoints LOSE 7-15% of games to a depth-4 alpha-beta baseline (aggregated over thousands of games, not noise): WL4 14.6%, WL5 7.1%, v6 mate-discount 10.1% vs lookahead:depth=4. A sophomore-grade exhaustive searcher out-CALCULATES our net in forcing lines. This is a TEACHING gap, not a capacity gap -- the same net draws pbrain-rapfi (~2625 on 9x9) near-100% of the time.

TARGET (Jason's framing): 100% win as black, 0% loss as white. Black (first player) is the forced-win side -> convert it. White (second player) can never WIN (strategy-stealing), so its only job is to never LOSE = force the draw. METRIC: loss-rate vs lookahead:depth=4 and depth=6 -> ~0, split by color.

WHY TEACHER/CURRICULUM, not runtime alpha-beta: AlphaZero only learns answers it is TAUGHT. A lost self-play game is already in the replay buffer, but labeled only z=-1 ("that whole game was bad") -- it never tells the net the move it SHOULD have played. VCF wins precisely because it stamps the EXACT right move. So the lever family is RELABEL the hard positions with the correct answer, not "show more positions" (the positions are already there).

DECOMPOSITION:
- ATTACK arm (100% black): extend the exact teacher from forced-fours (VCF, current champion) to forced-threes (VCT). Solver already BUILT (derby-1p5, commit 3a6c6d9). This epic ACTIVATES the existing deferred chain: derby-58f -> derby-y8r (fuzz gate) -> derby-rxf (wire --vct-teacher) -> derby-6us (race).
- DEFENSE arm (0% white): NEW. The current teacher proves forced wins for the side to move = attack only. It does NOT teach the defensive move that refuses to hand the opponent a forced win. Filed as the defensive-solver-teacher child bead.
- INSTRUMENT: color-split eval (child) so loss-rate can be measured black vs white -- this defines "done" for the defense arm.

RULED OUT (validated against the wiki -- do NOT re-try):
- Aux opponent-reply head: raced as the 'signal' lane in v4/v5, did NOT beat bare vcf head-to-head. Not the lever.
- Train-vs-baseline / --opponent-mix-random: already tried (pacifist_blocker, mix=0.5). Value-loss collapsed to 0.04 (defense-blindness). Making the OPPONENT stronger breaks training. The defense teacher gets the defensive signal WITHOUT this trap: pure self-play + exact RELABELING only.

ACCEPTANCE: a recipe combining VCT-attack + defense-teacher beats the vcf + global-pool + value-discount(0.98) base on BOTH (a) loss-rate vs lookahead:depth=4 and depth=6 (target -> 0, especially white-side) and (b) head-to-head delta-Elo. Measured with the color-split eval instrument.
acceptance_criteria: VCT-attack + defense-teacher recipe beats the vcf+global-pool+value-discount base on (a) loss-rate vs lookahead:depth=4 and depth=6 (target ->0, esp. white) and (b) head-to-head delta-Elo, measured with color-split eval.

and adds it as a second policy head loss scaled by `soft_policy_weight_scale` (a tuned
~O(0.1) auxiliary weight). KataGo added it precisely because peaked search targets

- ZERO generation cost. Our `pi` is ALREADY the Gumbel completed-Q policy target recorded in

title: WDL (win/draw/loss) value head -> land cell derby-x-wdl (CODE-ONLY, no GPU)
description:
LEVER + WHY  (Class-C model-arch fork — value-representation lever)
------------------------------------------------------------------
Replace the scalar tanh value head with a WDL (win/draw/loss) categorical head:
the net emits 3 logits -> softmax over {win, draw, loss}; everywhere the codebase
uses a scalar value it derives v = P(win) - P(loss). The SINGLE lever is "the value
REPRESENTATION" (scalar -> WDL); the existing value mechanisms (value-discount, VCF
value-stamp) are re-expressed NATIVELY in the new representation (defined exactly
below), NOT added as extra levers.

Source: AlphaGomoku (Kozarzewski) uses WDL as its PRIMARY value type (search/Value.hpp:
win_rate/draw_rate; getExpectation = win_rate + 0.5*draw_rate); KataGo's value subhead is
a WDL distribution; Leela Chess Zero's WDL head is the canonical writeup.

WHY for us: 9x9 freestyle games are ~60-70% DRAWS under strong two-sided defense
(research-board H2H draw rates: v4 ~50%, v5 ~65%, v6 ~60-70%). A scalar tanh value
squashes "solid draw" and "sharp 50/50 coin-flip" both to ~0.0, so the value head spends
most of its capacity regressing toward 0 in the draw-dominated middle and cannot tell a
dead-equal position from a double-edged one. A WDL head gives a confident (0,1,0) draw
target (cross-entropy) and exposes P(draw) that later cells can act on. Red-team verdict:
the highest Delta-elo/wall bet of the gomocup-AZ survey AND the only one that is purely
TRAINING-side -> it does NOT tax the Gumbel-SH generation hot path (value head is unchanged
in cost at self-play). Keystone that later unlocks draw-contempt + value-aware selection

title: Cross-game value sidecar -> land cell derby-x-crossgame (CODE-ONLY, no GPU)
description:
CODE-ONLY recipe for another session (the auto-factory). NO GPU run in this bead. Deliverable: land cell `derby-x-crossgame` in run_sweep.CELLS, available for the derby runner to swap in.

LEVER: cross-game value aggregation (a "position-stats sidecar"). Replace/blend the single-game value target z with a low-variance aggregate of outcomes across ALL games that passed through a position.

WHY: single-game +/-1 punishes a good move for a blunder that came 10 plies later -> the net sees contradictory labels for the same position and regresses to mushy ~0 values -> no killer instinct, no opening convergence. The v8 champions play DECISIVELY in self-play (Gumbel root = Sequential-Halving argmax, temperature/Dirichlet are discarded in the gumbel path, self_play.py:648,662), so the remaining source of value mush is precisely the single-game label. Aggregating across games de-noises the credit assignment -> confident values -> conversion. The opening is the most-transited region, so it gets the richest counts and should sharpen first.

PHASE 1 (THIS bead, CPU-only, runs beside the live derby):
- Canonical key: min over the 8 D4 symmetries of the board (reuse augment(), game.py:151). The board is already stored side-to-move-relative (board[0]=current player), so the key is side-relative and matches z's convention -> aggregation is correct by construction. Pack to ~20 bytes (two uint64 + uint16). No existing hash/zobrist in the repo; build it here.
- Trainer-owned SINGLE-WRITER store (no multi-process locking): the 8 self-play workers keep dropping atomic game-record .pt files exactly as today; the trainer aggregates on ingest. store = key -> {visits, sum_value}. COMPOSE WITH value-discount: each game contributes its discounted return 0.98^(plies_to_end)*z, so the aggregate is a Monte-Carlo discounted-value estimate.
- Recency-decay the counts (a poor-man's reanalyze, no GPU) to fight off-policy bias from old/weak-net games.
- Relabel on sample: store the canonical key as a ring-buffer column (compute once at ingest; ~30MB RAM at 1.5M). Read path = O(1) dict lookup; z_target = confidence-weighted blend(z_game, aggregate), gated by visit count (low-visit positions fall back to single-game z).
- Opt-in flags: --cross-game-value + --cross-game-store PATH. OFF = byte-identical baseline (aux-head discipline, model.py:37-47). Side-car file (e.g. latest.position_stats.pkl), NOT embedded in latest.pt; on resume load the sidecar, else rebuild from the buffer already embedded in latest.pt (~2 min).
- Tests: canonical-key D4-invariance; aggregate math; OFF-path byte-identical (param count + state_dict + a tiny smoke-gen identical); resume rebuild-from-buffer.
